dedupe_keys.name: internet society ixp success stories panama calgary bolivia guatemala and others

description: This Internet Society page collects short success stories of Internet exchange points and links to a fuller story for each. Examples on the page: Panama's InteRed, founded in 1997 and revived after a leadership change and donated equipment and training; the first Calgary IXP, built by volunteers on a shoestring budget after local traffic had been routed over 1,000 km to the United States; PIT Bolivia, born on 13 November 2013 with 90 Mbps of exchanged traffic, at 1.4 Gbps in February 2020 and now about 400 Gb of total traffic; and IXP.GT in Guatemala, exchanging traffic since November 2019 with ten participants. Producer: the Internet Society, whose IXP programme supports exchange points. Coverage: cases from the Americas and elsewhere. Access: a free public web page that links each full story. Licence and cost: not stated; free to read. Caveats: promotional summaries whose figures are quoted from the stories and not audited, and some page text was cut off in the read. Simulation uses: the growth and cost figures inform capacity-planning and agent-based models of IXP adoption. Related records: the ISOC assessment of IXP impact in Kenya and Nigeria (case_study-isoc-ixp-impact-kenya-nigeria-2012) and the Euro-IX IXP database (data-euro-ix-ixp-database).
